haiku-low.q1: No. Cursor updates never pass through the document service or Postgres. They go through the Redis cursor script and pub/sub channel only.
haiku-low.q2: At most one update per 50 ms per client. The node silently drops any cursor arriving less than 50 ms after the connection's last accepted cursor.
haiku-low.q3: It holds the cursor, keeping only the newest held cursor per connection, and draws it once that revision has been applied.
haiku-low.q4: It is drawn at transformPosition(pos, rev, appliedRev). If that throws HistoryGone, the position is dropped and that caret hidden until the next update.
haiku-low.q5: Each tab is a connection with its own caret. The user appears once: join is published only on first connection. Avatar removed only when userGone, meaning no other connections remain.
haiku-low.q6: After a clean tab close, well inside 2 s (milliseconds). After a node dies, at most 35 s, within the 45 s limit.
haiku-low.q7: Per document in Redis: conns hash, exp sorted set, cur hash. The owning node refreshes each live connection every 10 s, pushing expiry to now+30 s; keys have 60 s TTL.
haiku-low.q8: Every surviving node runs a sweep script every 5 s per document it has sockets on. It removes expired connections and publishes leave, which clients receive via the Redis channel.
haiku-low.q9: The accepted cursor is published on Redis channel presence:{docId}. Subscribed nodes deliver it to their local viewers. The document describes no separate same-node path.
haiku-low.q10: The client subscribes to presence:{docId} before running the join script and reading the snapshot, so no event falls in a gap. Duplicate events are harmless.
haiku-low.q11: The idle user's last cursor is stored in Redis cur:{docId}, so it arrives in the join snapshot. Clients also re-send cursors every 10 s if appliedRev moved.
haiku-low.q12: Each connection's cursor has a seq. The client ignores any seq at or below lastSeq, otherwise sets lastSeq = seq. The server stores and publishes only newer seq.

sonnet.q1: No. The cursor message never touches the document service or Postgres. It goes node -> Redis (cursor script stores it and publishes it).
sonnet.q2: A client sends at most one update per 50 ms, and always sends the final position when movement stops. The node silently drops any cursor that arrives less than 50 ms after the last one it accepted from that connection.
sonnet.q3: It holds the cursor, keeping only the newest held cursor per connection, and draws it once that revision has been applied.
sonnet.q4: It is drawn at transformPosition(pos, rev, appliedRev). If that throws HistoryGone, the client drops the position and hides that caret until the next update. Idle clients re-send every 10 s if appliedRev moved, to keep the stored rev within the editor's 500-revision history.
sonnet.q5: Each tab is its own connection, but the user appears once. Join is published only for the user's first connection, and the user's own client skips carets of its own user. The avatar is removed only when a leave has userGone true (no other connection remains). Each connection's caret is removed when that connection leaves.
sonnet.q6: Clean tab close: milliseconds, within the 2 s limit. Node death: at most 35 s (30 s expiry + 5 s sweep), within the 45 s limit.
sonnet.q7: In the existing Redis, per document and per connection (connId). The Redis hashes are conns:{docId} and cur:{docId}, and the sorted set is exp:{docId}. Each connection's expiry is pushed forward to now+30 s by its owning node every 10 s (after a ping answer, via the refresh script). The Redis keys also have a 60 s TTL reset on every write.
sonnet.q8: The entries stop being refreshed and expire 30 s after the last refresh. Every surviving node runs the sweep script every 5 s per document it has sockets on. The sweep removes expired connections and publishes leave events on the Redis pub/sub channel. The surviving nodes subscribed to the channel pass them to their clients. If no live node is left, the 60 s key TTL clears everything.
sonnet.q9: The cursor script publishes the cursor on the Redis pub/sub channel presence:{docId}. Every node subscribed to that document receives it and forwards it to its clients. For a viewer on the sender's own node, the document does not say whether delivery is a separate local path. The node is itself subscribed to the channel, so the document implies it receives the event the same way.
sonnet.q10: The node subscribes to presence:{docId} first, then runs the join script that returns the snapshot. So no event falls in a gap. An event may appear in both the snapshot and the channel, but applying it twice is harmless, so the client converges.
sonnet.q11: Each connection's last cursor is stored in Redis (cur:{docId}) and included in the join snapshot, so the idle user's caret arrives in the snapshot. The idle client also re-sends its cursor every 10 s if appliedRev has moved. The client sets lastSeq from the snapshot.
sonnet.q12: Per connection, the client keeps lastSeq. If a cursor's seq <= lastSeq it is ignored. Otherwise lastSeq is set to seq. The server's cursor script also stores and publishes only if seq is newer than the stored one.
